text:
maria.ops: FYI customer on Dedicated reported a restore that hung on decrypt for ~45m, ultimately succeeded after we retried. Logs show AccessDenied from KMS during part of the window. Any RBAC/KMS ideas?

sam.secops: Which snapshot id / region? Any cross-account copies involved?

maria.ops: snapshot: prod-eu-db-2026-03-19-03, region: eu-west-1. No cross-account copy reported by the UI. Here are the relevant log lines:

```
2026-03-19T03:12:45Z ERROR restore: decrypt failed, error=AccessDenied, keyId=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01
2026-03-19T03:58:12Z WARN  restore: retrying decrypt, grantId=gh-7890
2026-03-19T04:00:30Z INFO  restore: decrypt succeeded, duration=45m45s
```

liam-db: Are we using CMK per-tenant or a shared CMK for backups? If per-tenant CMK, RBAC scoping changes are more likely.

maria.ops: Per-tenant CMK. We did a permission tidy last week on backup-agent roles.

jordan.sre: First suspects: (1) ephemeral grant TTL expired during long restore, (2) IAM role change removed kms:Decrypt on the CMK, or (3) kms:ViaService condition failure for the S3/backup service. Check CloudTrail for KMS "Decrypt" failures and look for ListGrants/RetireGrant calls.

sam.secops: Also check if someone rotated CMK alias -> new keyId mismatch during restore window. Quick commands:

```
# list grants for key
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 --region eu-west-1

# cloudtrail lookup for decrypt errors
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-19T06:00:00Z
```

snapshot-bot: snapshot created by backup-agent@prod at 2026-03-19T02:58:00Z, kms_key_id=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01, grant_id=gh-7890

liam-db: If grant gh-7890 was issued with short TTL (we had a default of 30m for one-off grants in the old flow), that would explain a decrypt failing mid-restore. Restores that stream blobs can take longer than the grant TTL.

maria.ops: Can the backup service renew or request a longer grant during long restores? Current implementation requests a single grant at snapshot start.

jordan.sre: Short-term mitigation: issue a new grant for the CMK scoped to the backup-agent role with a longer TTL and retry a test restore. Medium-term: change grant issuance to cover expected max restore time or use an IAM role-based policy allowing kms:Decrypt from the backup service principal (with tight conditions).

sam.secops: I'm seeing an RBAC policy change in the audit log on 2026-03-18 22:14 UTC that removed kms:Decrypt for the backup-agent role on that CMK except when a grant is present. That was the intentional hardening, but we missed the restore-duration case.

maria.ops: Oof. So the policy intentionally forces grant usage but we have restores longer than the grant window.

liam-db: Plan: 1) Issue an emergency grant to cover current restores and validate customer restores. 2) Rewrap the affected snapshot to a CMK we manage for longer-lived restores (S3 copy with SSE-KMS to new key) as a customer-visible follow-up. 3) Update backup-agent to request longer grants for restore operations and add streaming renewals. 4) Add alerting when decrypt retries > X or when grant expiry happens mid-ops.

sam.secops: I'll issue a temporary grant now (ttl=6h) and post grant id. Also updating the RBAC change ticket to add exception language.

sam.secops: grant issued: gh-7901, TTL=6h, scope=backup-agent role.

maria.ops: Retried restore for affected customer after grant gh-7901 and it completed in ~6m. Customer notified and updated. :thumbsup:

jordan.sre: For postmortem: we should capture metrics on restore durations per snapshot size and integrate them into the grant TTL defaults. Also add a pre-restore check to ensure an active grant or IAM policy will allow decrypt for the expected duration.

liam-db: I'll handle the rewrap for that snapshot tomorrow and leave a ticket with the customer-visible timeline.

sam.secops: Filed follow-up tickets: ENGOPS-1287 (grant-renewal + defaults), RBAC-452 (policy exception language), PM-331 (customer communication update).

maria.ops: Thanks all. Quick action minimized customer impact. Leaving this open for the follow-ups.

jordan.sre: One more note — add CloudTrail alerts for KMS AccessDenied spikes and correlate with snapshot restores so we can auto-open incident playbook if it recurs.

maria.ops: Agree. Tagging this resolved-for-now, will reopen if we see repeats. :white_check_mark:
